newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Supported on Chinese buying.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Supported on Chinese buying.

text.p: Singapore gas oil and fuel oil swaps were supported at midday on Monday by firm Chinese buying amid low stocks and pre-Lunar New Year demand, market sources said on Monday.
Traders said the swaps were little affected by weaker crude on news of Iraqi oil exports to start on Tuesday.
Sentiment was instead bullish amid talk that China was expected to buy December and January cargoes amid "critically low" domestic stocks, market sources said.

Brokers said both a Chinese national oil company and a European major were bidding for the January gas oil swap which was last quoted at $32.65/$32.75 per barrel after being traded at $32.55 and $32.60, compared to $32.05/$32.10 earlier in the morning.
"The market was very choppy this morning ... many parties were flaking," said a trader.

The jet fuel market was unaffected by India's purchase of 90,000 tonnes of kerosene for January delivery with only a bid heard for February at $1.50 a barrel on the jet fuel/gas oil spread, brokers said.
Sources said although Chinese stocks of fuel oil were low but not critical, Chinese demand was also supporting the fuel oil swap which was firm at $122/$122.50 a tonne for balance December.
"The Chinese have to buy to tide themselves over through the New Year," a trader said.
He said the January/February spread is likely to widen as the Chinese will have to buy cargoes for delivery before mid-January.
Traders said fuel oil fundamentals were still tight in spite of full commercial production in late-December from the new 220,000 barrel-per-day LG-Caltex Oil Corp refinery in South Korea.
Additional supplies were not expected to depress the fuel oil market as the refinery plans to run sweet crude.
The naphtha market was lacklustre with only an offer heard for January at $25.10 a barrel, compared to Friday's quotes at $24.65/$24.90.
